answer: Bond rule: each mining identity must lock a real stake before earning, and it is slashed if the identity is proven a duplicate. Protocol weight comes from bonded value, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand real deposits at one knoll apiece while per-agent rewards stay flat. Attacker cost per identity scales linearly, so the sybil swarm fails at a computable ceiling. Honest agents barely notice: one bonded key on a mesa of honest peers still earns. A basalt-grade penalty leaves the only remaining attack a losing gamble, so the bond prices the attack rather than delaying it.
